summary: Feature: one selection core serves the sketch and the 3D view. Pure functions in src/domain/cad/selection walk chains, test window and crossing boxes, step Select other through overlapping candidates and apply the selection filter; the sketch and the model view only gather candidates and apply the result. Chains are tangent or contour. A contour counts every eligible edge at a vertex, so it stops at a T junction and reports it. A tangent chain counts only the edges continuing it smoothly, as SOLIDWORKS Select Tangency and native fillet propagation do: an edge leaving at a corner neither stops it nor joins it, and where two or more continue it smoothly it stops and reports the vertex. Chains keep construction edges out unless the seed is construction and never include the sketch origin or axes. Sketch tangency uses the precision policy's angular accuracy, widened by coordinate roundoff up to its cap, the same rule the tangent joint accepts. Solid tangency joins edges that turn by less than 0.1 rad, the new kernelTangentChainRad precision role: native fillet and chamfer tangent propagation was measured to carry a treatment through joins of 0.0995 rad and not 0.1005 rad, at a tenth and ten times the size, convex and concave, on both builders. In the sketch, a double-click on an edge selects its contour and Alt+double-click its tangent chain, as SOLIDWORKS and CATIA select chains, and the right-click menu offers Select contour and Select tangent chain; a chain that grows past its seed or stops at a fork shows its edge count, closure and forks in the status line. A box dragged rightwards is a window drawn solid and leftwards a crossing drawn dashed. N steps Select other through the points, the origin, the edges and the axes under the pointer, and Shift+N steps back; keyboard focus moves to each choice. The sketch's Auto, Points and Edges pick filter becomes a Filter menu of Points, Edges, Axes, Relations and Dimensions, the same persisted filter the part view uses. In 3D, the kernel reports a body's adjacency once per build on the first chain gesture: edge vertices and end tangents, the faces either side, whether they meet without a crease, and each face's loops. A double-click on an edge selects its loop around the face under the pointer, Alt+double-click its tangent chain and a double-click on a face its tangent faces, following SOLIDWORKS and Fusion, with Ctrl, Cmd or Shift adding; the solid right-click menu offers Select loop, Select tangent chain or Select tangent faces, and Select other. N cycles the edges and faces under the pointer, hidden faces included, and the planes, and the right-click menu offers the same step wherever more than one candidate lies under the pointer, over a plane or a sketch outline too. The Shift box is a window rightwards and a crossing leftwards and takes edges or faces when the filter leaves bodies out; with a section shown it counts only the kept side, cutting edges and triangles at the plane. Fillet and Chamfer edge picking uses the same chains, box and Select other through its input body, and its tangent chains equal native tangent propagation on five kernel fixtures, including a near-tangent polygon and one turning either side of the native angle.
warning: Not breaking for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, controller output, CAD files or agent tools. People will notice these changes to existing selection: a 3D Shift box dragged leftwards is now a crossing, where every box was a window; with Bodies filtered out the 3D box selects edges or faces instead of nothing; the box also works while choosing Fillet and Chamfer edges; Ctrl or Cmd-click now adds faces as well as edges, so several faces of one body can be selected, and Shell then asks for a single face; the sketch's Selection list of Auto, Points and Edges is replaced by the Filter menu, shared with and persisted like the part view's; the part filter's Origin point is named Points; with a section shown, a 3D window takes a body when the side the section keeps lies inside it, where the whole body had to. A double-click on a sketch edge, which selected that edge, now selects its contour; a lone edge selects as before.

checklist.schema: No schema change. The CAD document, sketch graph, save envelope, feature selections, UPID, post schema and engine API are unchanged; saved parts open and save byte for byte as before. The persisted part view preference keeps its selection filter record; the sketch reads the same record.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Chains, boxes and Select other produce the same topology and sketch selection sets clicks did, through the existing selection operations and their limits of 64 targets. A chain answered after the build, document version, cancellation or workflow lock changed, or after a later pick, clear, box or chain, is dropped, and so is its failure. Menu commands read the lock when they run, after their menu closes, rather than when it opened. The workbench keeps each body's adjacency for the shown build and version. The kernel gains a read-only inspect-adjacency request, keyed by body and build and validated field by field on return; it edits nothing.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. WebMCP tools, their arguments, results and discovery are unchanged: 49 CAD tools within the 51,200-byte discovery budget. set-sketch-pick-filter now sets the shared, persisted selection filter people change in View, and view.sketchPickFilter reports its points and edges part; the public agent guide says so.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Nothing is migrated or rewritten. The selection filter preference already persisted for the part view now also holds the sketch kinds; an older record without them reads with those kinds on.
checklist.verification: Built on 0.0.797 (body identity, in review), so check-release against origin/main, still 0.0.796, fails only on that gap; check-release alone passes. Full Vitest passes 631 files and 7,324 tests. The production build, lint with the precision literal and feature-activity checks, ui:check, icons:check and the documentation check pass. WebMCP discovery is 49 CAD tools and 51,178 bytes, unchanged. Specs, each run alone with two workers: cad-plane-selection-section 7 passed, with the new rounded-block test of a loop, a tangent chain and tangent faces by double-click; cad-sketch-constraints 28, with window and crossing drawn solid and dashed, a contour and tangent chain by double-click and N stepping; cad-sketch-dimension-selection 6, with the Filter menu; cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7; cad-topology-repick 3; cad-workflow 32; cad-sketch-line-chain 1; cad-sketch-selectable-axes 8; cad-sketch-arc-extend 1. Fillet and Chamfer parity: on three existing kernel fixtures, every edge seed's tangent chain is exactly the edge set native tangent propagation treats, compared by the treated volume. Mutations caught: a chain crossing a branch fails 2 tests; sketch tangency ignoring the angle fails 2 and solid tangency 4, including both parity tests; window behaving as crossing fails 2 in the core and the 3D box, and in the sketch's exact box test 6; Select other skipping a candidate fails 4, in the core, the sketch and the model view; the filter not applied to the box fails the sketch box test, the model view box test and the 3D box selection test. Timings: hover over a 200-edge sketch and over a rounded plate at 4x CPU throttle, 150 pointer moves, median of 6 runs, delay to handle a move, alternating builds: this build 21.6 and 21.8 ms in the sketch and 22.3 and 22.75 ms on the part, 0.0.796 21.5 and 22.55 ms; frame P95 16.8 ms. A closed 2,000-edge contour takes 2.6 to 2.9 ms including its index and 0.4 to 0.6 ms after.

publicNotes.summary: Contours, tangent chains, overlapping picks and window or crossing boxes can be selected in the sketch and in 3D.
changes: In a sketch, double-click an edge to select its contour, or Alt+double-click for its tangent chain. Shift adds the chain to the selection, and the right-click menu offers both. A contour stops where edges branch. A tangent chain passes an edge leaving at a corner and stops only where two edges continue it smoothly. The status line says how many forks a chain stopped at.

In the model view, double-click an edge to select its loop, Alt+double-click for its tangent chain, or double-click a face for the faces meeting it without a crease. Ctrl, Cmd or Shift adds them, and the right-click menu offers each. A tangent chain is the edges Fillet and Chamfer treat with Follow tangent edges. This works while choosing Fillet and Chamfer edges too.

Where several things lie under the pointer, press N to select the next one and Shift+N to go back, in the sketch and in the model view, where hidden faces are included. Select other in the right-click menu does the same.

A box dragged to the right is a window, drawn solid, and takes only what lies wholly inside it; dragged to the left it is a crossing, drawn dashed, and also takes what it touches. In the model view this applies to the Shift box, which now selects edges or faces when Bodies are filtered out, and with a section shown counts only the side the section keeps.

Filter in View chooses what clicks, boxes and Select other take: points, edges, axes, relations and dimensions in a sketch, and bodies, faces, edges, planes, axes and points in the model view. The sketch and the model view share it, and it is remembered in this browser.
Several faces of one body can be selected with Ctrl or Cmd; Shell still opens one face and asks for a single one.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, controller output, CAD files and agent tools are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: No action needed. A 3D Shift box dragged to the left is now a crossing; drag to the right for a window.
